summary: Frontend-only verification of Customer Expo-web guest OTP flow + two UI fixes (home scroll, customer bottom nav gradient). 5 of 6 checks fully PASS; 1 real bug found in phone paste normalization; wrong-OTP path could not be exercised in dev because the send-OTP endpoint returns dev_otp which is auto-verified within milliseconds (not a functional bug, but the negative path is not user-reachable in dev).

ui_bugs.issue: Paste of '+91 98765 43210' does NOT normalize to '9876543210'. The TextInput has maxLength={10}; the browser truncates the pasted value to the first 10 characters ('+91 98765 ') BEFORE onChangeText fires, so tenDigits() only receives 7 digits and phone becomes '9198765'. The last-10-digits logic on line 19 of OtpInline.tsx is defeated by the maxLength attribute. Fix: remove maxLength from the TextInput and instead clamp inside onChangeText (already done), OR raise maxLength to ~16 so full pasted E.164 strings survive to the handler.

action_items: Fix OtpInline phone paste normalization: remove or raise maxLength on the otp-phone TextInput so the tenDigits(v).slice(-10) logic can actually receive pasted '+91 xxxxx xxxxx' style inputs.

(Optional) In dev, consider delaying auto-verify by ~500ms or NOT auto-filling from dev_otp so QA can exercise the wrong-OTP error path via UI. Currently /auth/send-otp returns dev_otp which is stored into state and immediately verified by the length===6 useEffect, leaving no window for a manual wrong entry.
critical_code_review_comments: OtpInline.tsx line 69: maxLength={10} conflicts with the intent stated in the comment on line 18 ('Keep the LAST 10 digits so pasted +91… still resolves'). Either drop maxLength or bump it to accept the full pasted string.
OtpInline.tsx line 39: setOtp(String(d.dev_otp)) triggers auto-verify via the useEffect on line 61. This is intentional for happy path, but blocks negative-path testing in dev.

rca of the issue: T3 paste bug RCA: OtpInline.tsx line 69 sets maxLength={10} on <TextInput testID="otp-phone">. In web, this maps to HTMLInputElement.maxLength=10; browser truncates any pasted text to 10 raw characters BEFORE dispatching input events. onChangeText then receives '+91 98765 ' (with spaces), and tenDigits('+91 98765 ') filters non-digits yielding '9198765'. Reproduction: on /book Step 4 Your Info, focus the phone input and paste '+91 98765 43210' → observed value '9198765' (expected '9876543210'). Mitigation: remove the maxLength prop (already handled inside onChangeText via slice(-10)) OR set maxLength={16} so the E.164 form survives to the handler.
